title: Ankhwennefer
capsule: Ankhwennefer (Chaonnophris in Greek sources) was a rebel pharaoh of Upper Egypt who succeeded Horwennefer around 200 BCE and sustained the great Egyptian revolt against Ptolemaic rule in the Thebaid until approximately 186 BCE. He exploited the Ptolemies' preoccupation with the Fifth Syrian War (202–195 BCE) to consolidate control of Upper Egypt, recruiting Nubian auxiliaries and maintaining a separate royal titulature invoking Osiris. The Ptolemaic general Comanus retook Thebes in 191 BCE and continued the reconquest; Ankhwennefer was captured around 186 BCE after his son died in the final battle, with Egyptian priests reportedly interceding to spare his life. Ptolemy V's amnesty decree helped restore Ptolemaic legitimacy in the south.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Ankhwennefer's reign is attested through demotic papyri, hieroglyphic inscriptions at Philae, and Greek papyri giving regnal dates, but the exact chronology and territorial limits of the rebellion within Upper Egypt remain areas of scholarly debate.
